- Confirm whether procurement wants the 24-month term or prefers 12+renewal?
- Share any redlines from legal (track changes preferred) — I attached a clean copy and the order form.

From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@northbridge.com>

Cc: NorthBridge Procurement <contracts@northbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:42:12 -0700
Subject: Re: NorthBridge renewal: initial draft and order form

Marissa —

Thanks for sending. I reviewed at a high level and sent the draft to our legal and procurement teams. Procurement will coordinate a short redline but flagged a few commercial items up front:
- Procurement prefers a 24-month term but wants a one-time termination right at month 12 for material breach only.
- They want SLA credit language to be quantitative and capped (we propose 30 days of credit cap per year).
- We will push back on indemnity language if it includes third-party patent claims — we need clearer carve-outs.

I attached a marked-up version (NB_Redline_MSA_v3.docx) with inline comments from legal and procurement contact details. Contracts will be the primary negotiator — copying them.

Also: procurement asked whether the capacity addendum can separate baseline vs. burst capacity for billing clarity.


On a separate note: is Redwood able to provide a short SOC2 evidence packet (summary only) we can attach to the purchase file? Procurement will ask before final signatures.

Best,
Nora Patel
Director, Finance Operations
NorthBridge Labs
nora.patel@northbridge.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NorthBridge renewal: initial draft and order form

Marissa — thanks for the loop. I reviewed Nora's redline and pulled out the items we should consider accepting vs. pushback. Summary below so legal has a clean checklist for review:

Summary of Nora / procurement asks (from NB_Redline_MSA_v3.docx):
1) Term: accept 24 months; add a defined cure period and limit early termination to material breach only (we can accept but clarify notice/cure timelines).
2) SLA credits: replace vague "credit at our discretion" language with explicit formulas (e.g., credit = percentage of monthly fee per incident) and a per-year cap; agree to the concept but propose cap at 15 days of credits per year rather than 30.
3) Indemnity: remove sweeping third-party patent carve-outs; propose retaining server-side IP carve-outs and add mutual indemnity for data/privacy claims — legal to draft scoped language.
4) Capacity addendum: split baseline (committed) vs. burst (overage pricing). We should accept separation and add Exhibit A table with baseline QPS and burst pricing tiers. Attach ExhibitA_Capacity_Addendum.xlsx for review.
5) Data residency / SOC2 evidence: provide redacted SOC2 summary plus our SOC2 report URL; limit evidence to redacted report and SOC2 control summary.
6) Sign path: DocuSign preferred by procurement. We should prepare a single DocuSign room combining MSA + Exhibit A + Order Form; Lauren, can Legal Ops create the room and set signatories?

Proposed commercial trade-offs to accept now to keep momentum:
- Accept 24-month term with the material-breach-only 12-month exit and a 30-day cure period.
- Compromise SLA cap to 15 days of credits/year but tighten the SLA formula language.
- Accept separation of baseline vs burst but hold on rate tiers until we confirm expected burst volumes.

Next steps (suggested):
- Kimberly: fold Jordan's bullets into a redline and produce a "clean redline" with tracked block text for MSA sections 4 (Term), 7 (SLA), 11 (Indemnity), Exhibit A.
- Lauren: open DocuSign room and draft signatory template (CEO + Procurement head).
- Marissa: confirm whether NB's procurement will accept our reduced SLA-credit cap or insist on 30 days.

If we move quickly we can have legal's counter to Nora by EOD Wednesday and aim to send DocuSign by next Tuesday.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Manager, Renewals (Redwood Inference)
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@northbridge.com>, NorthBridge Procurement <contracts@northbridge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NorthBridge renewal: redlines, term proposal & sign path

Nora / Contracts team —

Really appreciate the quick turn. We're aligned on the high-level approach and want to keep this moving so it hits your May 1 target. Quick recap and plan: 

- Term: Redwood accepts 24-month term. We'll add a 30-day written cure period and restrict early termination at month 12 to material breach with process outlined in section 4.
- SLA credits: we will propose a tightened formula and a 15-day annual cap (happy to show math). If procurement cannot accept 15 days, we'll escalate for an exception review.
- Indemnity: legal will produce scoped mutual indemnity language; we will not accept unlimited third-party patent exposure.
- Capacity addendum: I've attached ExhibitA_Capacity_Addendum.xlsx (baseline vs burst). Please confirm baseline QPS and expected monthly burst so we can finalize tiered pricing.
- SOC2 evidence: Kimberly will send a redacted SOC2 summary and a link to the SOC2 overview page for your procurement packet.

Sign path: per Jordan's suggestion, Lauren will create a DocuSign room that contains the MSA + Exhibit A + Order Form. HubSpot deal id NB-2027-045 is updated with the proposed signers (CEO, Head of Procurement).

DocuSign link (provisional): https://www.docusign.com/rooms/abcdef123456
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/6789012

Can Contracts confirm two things by EOD Friday so we can issue a legal counter: 1) whether the 15-day SLA credit cap is acceptable or 30 days is required, and 2) the email addresses of the final signatories for DocuSign (full name + title).

Thanks — I'll hold off on a legal counter until we hear back on those two points.

Best,
Marissa Cole
